title: Chapter 5 · Storage and Upgrades
subtitle: Store MRU and carry it with you

blocks.text: The purer the quartz, the more MRU it will hold. Fill one and carry it, and away from home your staffs and charms will have something to draw on.
Goal: refine Nether quartz, tier by tier, into MRU crystals in the Magician Table. The soul storage on the next page is made from them, and the bigger the storage, the higher the tier it calls for.
Every tier uses only the middle slot, one for one, which makes it easy to feed with hoppers ([[crafting/magician_table]]).

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: You made your first MRU Shard.

blocks.title: What this chapter takes
blocks.text: The one thing this chapter can't do without is the Red Soul Matter in the Charging Chamber recipe. It takes 4 MRU Chunks, a little over 3,000 MRU counting from quartz. Bring about 10 quartz, and with a Heat Generator running you'll have it in a few minutes.

Goal: make a soul storage item to keep MRU in and carry around. The forebears gave soul storage its name, and the first MRU they kept in it was MRU drawn from their own matrices. These items work like batteries. When the staffs, charms and magic gear of later chapters need MRU, they take it from the soul storage on you.
How to use it

Keep it in your inventory, your offhand or a ring slot of your accessory bar. The accessory bar comes from the Curios mod and sits on your inventory screen. MRU is taken from the accessory slots first, then your inventory, then your offhand, and only when all the soul storage on you adds up to enough. Creative mode takes nothing.
Keep it in your inventory or your offhand. MRU is taken from your inventory first, then your offhand, and only when all the soul storage on you adds up to enough. Creative mode takes nothing.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: You've made any one of them. It starts out empty, and the Charging Chamber on the next page fills it.

blocks.title: Which first
blocks.text: The Charging Chamber itself needs a {item:essentialcraft5:red_soul_matter}, so make that one first. {item:essentialcraft5:matter_of_eternity} needs a Nether star, so leave it until you've beaten the Wither.
Later on, Matter of Eternity also goes into the [[hologram/holopad]], so start saving Nether stars early.
Goal: build a {item:essentialcraft5:charging_chamber} to charge your soul storage.

Prepare: one {item:essentialcraft5:red_soul_matter}, which can be empty, 2 {item:essentialcraft5:magic_plate}, and one each of {item:essentialcraft5:magical_screen}, {item:essentialcraft5:mru_conversion_matrix}, {item:essentialcraft5:matrix_link}, {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_frame}, {item:essentialcraft5:mru_catcher} and {item:essentialcraft5:elemental_core}.
How to use it

items: Place the chamber and put in a Bound Gem linked to a generator.
Put the item to charge in its item slot.
When the MRU in the item's tooltip is full, take it out and carry it.

rows: Up to 1/20 of the item's capacity per tick, but never faster than the source refills it
For every 1 MRU charged into the item, the chamber spends {cfg:machines.charging_chamber.charge_cost_modifier} MRU
Anything that stores MRU: soul storage, and later staffs and magic tools

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: You have a Charging Chamber. Put soul storage in and the MRU in its tooltip starts climbing.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: In the end, charging is only as fast as the source produces. One Heat Generator with lava on all sides takes about 6 minutes to fill a Red Soul Matter. For big items, bind more generators or let it charge while you do other things.
Hoppers and pipes can put items into the item slot and pull them out again, but <w>they pull whether the item is full or not</w>. With a plain hopper underneath, things leave as soon as they go in.
Charging the armor you wear

When the player who placed the chamber stands right on top of it, it charges the MRU-holding armor they wear. The item slot and the worn pieces take turns, one per tick, each charged at the same rate and loss as the item slot. Your body's center has to be over the block; leaning out over the next block doesn't count. With two chambers stacked, standing on top only counts for the upper one. Nobody else gets charged.
That way you don't have to take the armor off.
While you wear armor that blocks damage with MRU, a small box left of the hotbar shows how much charge the pieces have left in all ([[gear/mhs_armor]]).
Goal: reach matrix rank 2, Drawing. From this rank on, you can hold MRU in yourself.
You need

rows: 8 kinds in all, 2 of them Nether mobs
20,000 UBMRU, plus 2,000 MRU in the Crucible

cells: 3 in all, up to 2 at once; 32 health each, 5 damage a hit; 80 seconds

blocks.text: How

items: Go to the Nether and kill 2 kinds of Nether mob. Zombified piglins, piglins, magma cubes, ghasts, blazes and wither skeletons all count; [[matrix/codex]] lists all nine.
Bank UBMRU in your trial reserve bit by bit as for rank 1, until you have 20,000.
Place the offerings in the Crucible's offering slots and fill it with enough MRU through a Bound Gem.
Stand within 3 blocks with your bound Soul Stone in your main hand, open the screen, and once everything on the right is ticked, start the trial.

items.text: Defeat enough Matrix Echoes, and don't stray far from the Crucible.
Stay next to the Crucible without moving or getting hurt until the channel finishes.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: "Rank 2 · Drawing" appears in the middle of the screen, and your Soul Stone's tooltip shows matrix rank 2.

Rank 2 gives you a [[matrix/reservoir|Matrix Reservoir]] holding {cfg:general.matrix_rank.pool_per_rank|mul:1} MRU. Your UBMRU slowly converts into it by itself, and this mod's carried items draw on it once your soul storage runs low.

blocks.title: Mobs out of reach
blocks.text: Ghasts and blazes often hang in the air where a sword can't reach. A bow does the job, or you can make a [[guns/pistol]] from the side chapter on magical guns.
Goal (optional): install an upgrade in the Magician Table so it crafts faster. The forebears found their tables slow and often set a piece of alloy or crystal into them.

items: Right-click the table with an upgrade item in hand to install it. One leaves your hand and sits in the table.
A table holds one upgrade at a time, so take the old one out before you swap. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand and it pops out on top of the table, unharmed.
Once installed, the table's screen shows its current speed multiplier.

blocks.text: An upgrade multiplies the progress the table makes each tick, and its MRU use per tick by the same factor. A craft costs the same total MRU and just finishes sooner, provided your source keeps up.
An installed upgrade always comes back out as it went in, so you lose nothing by slotting a precious core in for now. Just take it out before you craft with it.

rows: A Chapter 3 part made from iron, Elemental Gems and one ender pearl

blocks.title: Which one now
blocks.text: Go with the Eye of Absorption, which is faster than Ender Scale Alloy and much cheaper. You'll still make Ender Scale Alloy, because Chapter 6's Combined Magical Alloys use it.
Ender Scale Alloy takes a {item:essentialcraft5:magic_fortified_plating} in the middle and an ender pearl in each corner, for 1,000 MRU.
That's the early game done

The next chapter moves on to mid-game materials, and the table suddenly gets much busier. Chapter 6 alone needs close to 20,000 points of progress. Before you go on, add a generator or two and fit the table with an Eye of Absorption.
The basics of MRU, Balance, MRUCUs and corruption are collected in two Getting Started pages, [[start/mru]] and [[start/mrucu]].
